subject.title: fix #95279: Provide a trusted inbound-decoration contract so consumers can strip/dedup without forgeable text heuristics

question: Should OpenClaw accept top-level inboundDecorated and bareBody as the durable serialized user-message contract for trusted inbound decoration, or require the same data under an OpenClaw-owned metadata envelope before merge?
rationale: The code path is coherent, but the permanent location of trusted session-message metadata is a compatibility-sensitive product/API boundary that tests cannot settle.

options.title: Accept Top-Level Fields
options.body: Accept inboundDecorated and bareBody as additive serialized message fields and proceed with exact-head validation and normal merge review.

options.title: Require Metadata Envelope
options.body: Ask the author to keep the same resolver and tests but store the trusted marker and body under an approved OpenClaw-owned metadata object before merge.

options.title: Defer To Alternate Contract
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want the separate raw-body or plugin-hook work to define the durable inbound body contract first.

recommendation.title: Accept Top-Level Fields
recommendation.body: Accept inboundDecorated and bareBody as additive serialized message fields and proceed with exact-head validation and normal merge review.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent merged history across inbound metadata stripping and hardening in the affected paths.
